fresh_checks.checked_reasoning: The maximum-point estimate is u_beta <= f+n log(1+A)/beta. Fix delta and a smooth strict v_j uniformly within delta/2 of p before beta tends to infinity. Its positive density lower bound c_j may depend on j; C_j=max(0,-log c_j) gives the exponential subsolution. No uniform c_j or background closedness is used.

Uniform convergence plus exponential density decay on compact subsets of the open gap proves support through bounded Bedford--Taylor continuity. The continuity of p is the earlier continuous-envelope result, independent of this approximation.

Uniform smooth obstacle approximation uses the envelope Lipschitz estimate. Inf-convolution gives Lipschitz f_j increasing to bounded lower semicontinuous f with common bounds. For fixed k, the open set {p_infinity<f_k} has zero measure for every large j; fixed-background increasing convergence and the open-set weak-limit inequality preserve zero mass.

Choquet regularization adds only a countable pluripolar exception. The limiting envelope lies below P(f), and its measure vanishes on the strict gap. Previously proved bounded domination identifies it with P(f); no final measure identification is assumed in this step.

Lower semicontinuous obstacles decrease quasi-everywhere to f. For fixed k, the bounded coefficient min(1,(f-p_k)_+) is quasi-continuous and annihilates every sufficiently late measure. Weighted capacity convergence passes the identity to the limit; the gap sets increase.

theta_j=theta+omega/j is Hermitian and the bounded envelopes decrease to P_theta(f). Every potential is bounded for the fixed theta+omega background. Expanding mixed products and using uniform capacity bounds also passes the quasi-continuous weighted identity.

Capping the obstacle above sup p changes neither envelope nor its contact set. Lower truncations admit constant competitors. Fixed H_k,C=min(1,(f-p_k)_+)min(1,(p+C)_+) selects levels on which truncation locality applies. Two exhaustions and continuity from below permit infinite total mass.

Support on p=min(u,v) is partitioned into {p=u<v} and {p=v}; common contact contributes once. Ordered contact applies on common finite levels. The arbitrary big-background contact theorem is a forward cited input, not a newly completed Chapter13 proof review.

fresh_checks.topic: Finite mass of model fixed points
fresh_checks.checked_reasoning: For phi=P_theta[phi]<=0 the rooftop P_theta(phi+1,0) equals phi. Its first contact set is contained in the pole set and contributes no extended mass. The zero-obstacle term gives MA(phi)<=1_{phi=0} theta^n.

Choose theta_rho>=a omega with rho<=0. The obstacle u-rho is bounded below and finite almost everywhere, so its Hermitian envelope p is bounded. On p+rho=u, positivity and ordered contact transfer the strictly positive bounded Hermitian mass to u. This gives individual positivity without a common lower bound.
For bounded u,v, w_b=P_theta(bu-(b-1)v) is bounded. The convex potential w_b/b+(1-1/b)v contacts u. If (1-1/b)^n>c, its contact measure vanishes where u<v. Positive total mass then gives sup w_b>=-C.

The fixed strict gap E={u<v-a} has positive volume even though it need not be open. On E the obstacle forces w_b<=C-(b-1)a outside a pluripolar exception, so its normalized L1 norm diverges. Fixed-background normalized compactness contradicts this; uniform lower mass is unnecessary.

Both extended volume extrema run over v ordinarily equivalent to u, rather than over a single mass or an ideal type. Smooth gauge change v->v-f preserves the currents and measures; positive scaling is a competitor bijection and gives t^n. For semipositive theta, v_-(theta)>0 is stronger than individual non-collapsing.

A_b is defined by the convex inequality h/b+(1-1/b)phi<=u. For b=1 it means h<=u. This avoids subtracting common infinities. Nonempty families have a finite-sublevel upper bound and genuine upper envelope; canonical almost-everywhere order makes the convex inequality pointwise.

For u>=phi-C, use phi-bC. A bounded downward change of u is absorbed by h-bC. Convex combinations, upward changes within u preceq phi and maxima preserve membership. Replacing phi by an ordinarily equivalent reference is absorbed by h-(b-1)C. Smooth gauge subtracts f from every term.

Q_bs(u,phi) supplies every s-stretch competitor for Q_b(u,phi) when u<=phi. For u<=w with both in the class, a common translation below phi gives Q_b(u,phi)<=Q_b(u,w)<=u<=phi and upward stability. Convex inequalities extend across poles.

For N members translated below phi, the average of Q_N(u_i,phi) is a common competitor and lies in the relative class. The resulting rooftop belongs to the class by upward stability. The sequence phi-j shows that countably infinite rooftops can collapse to minus infinity; no sequence closure is asserted.

For a in (0,1), choose a phi+(1-a)h_a<=u. Combining obstacle competitors gives a P_F[phi]+(1-a)P_F[h_a]<=P_F[u]. P[h_a] has supremum zero; obstacle translation and normalized compactness bound P_F[h_a] uniformly in L1. Letting a increase to one proves ordinary-envelope equality, without an ideal-envelope or finite-mass conclusion.

The positive-mass section assumes theta semipositive and big, phi an ordinary envelope fixed point and P_{epsilon theta}(phi) genuine for one epsilon in (0,1). The comparison with the positive-lower-volume condition is explicitly assigned to the bounded-mass regime.

For u<=phi<=0, w=P_theta(u-phi) is genuine, at most zero, and w+phi<=u. A stretch competitor h_b satisfies h_b<=b(u-phi); semipositivity makes h_b/b theta-plurisubharmonic, giving h_b<=bw and w in E_env(theta,0). Pole sets do not require evaluating a difference of infinities.

If q=P_{a theta}(u) is genuine, then p=P_{(1-a)theta}(u-q) is bounded. Contact support and positive mixed products transfer its mass to u on p+q=u. Scaling p=(1-a)tilde p gives (1-a)^n v_-(theta), while bigness supplies separate strictly positive individual mass even when v_-=0.

fresh_checks.topic: Positive mass throughout the relative class
fresh_checks.checked_reasoning: For 0<delta<1-epsilon, P_{epsilon theta}(phi)+delta P_theta(w/delta)<=phi+w<=u supplies a genuine competitor in (epsilon+delta)theta. Letting delta decrease to zero gives the uniform lower estimate; one fixed delta gives individual positivity. The extended mass may remain infinite.

The previously reviewed witness U=sum 2^{-j}u_j has a smooth head A_N and a genuine tail V_N in PSH(2^{-N}omega). For each b>1 choose b 2^{-N}<=1. Then bV_N+min(bA_N) is omega-plurisubharmonic and <=bU. The same argument works for epsilon U with b epsilon 2^{-N}<=1.

The witness lies in E_env(omega,0), hence has ordinary envelope zero. Its infinite mass and all-weight trivial multiplier ideals retain the earlier Chapter6 proof scope. This does not conflict with the finite mass of the fixed point zero, and does not claim that representatives of a fixed envelope have finite mass.

Bounded mass implies finite extended mass for every omega-plurisubharmonic potential by the earlier proposition. Failure of bounded mass supplies the witness in the relative class with ordinary envelope zero, contradicting each asserted universal finiteness condition. No formal open question is closed.
